title: Sep 16 Results + Sep 17 Preview: When 73% Feels Like Pure Magic
summary: 11-4 on Sep 16 with standout performances. Tomorrow: Brewers return to Pittsburgh.

content.value:
## Here's the Thing About Yesterday

Sometimes you wake up, check the scores, and just smile. September 16th was one of those days. An 11-4 record with 73.3% accuracy—the kind of performance that makes you believe in the process all over again.

The model had conviction yesterday, and more often than not, that conviction paid off. From Cleveland to Tampa Bay, we watched favorites hold serve and a few underdogs make their case. Let's break down what happened.

## The Wins That Made Our Day

The Guardians came through at home with 61% confidence—one of our stronger plays that delivered. Same story in Milwaukee, where the Brewers took care of business in Pittsburgh at 61% probability.

The Phillies-Nationals game? That 60% pick on Philadelphia felt right from the start, and the Orioles did their thing against the Mets at 59%. Even the Giants managed to edge out the Cardinals in what was basically a coin flip at 51%.

The Cubs hosting the Braves was another 61% winner, and watching that one unfold reminded me why we trust the numbers even when the matchup feels tricky.

## The Misses We're Learning From

No sugarcoating it—the Yankees and Dodgers didn't come through. Both were 54% and 61% picks respectively, and both reminded us that baseball has a beautiful way of humbling even the best models.

The Yankees-Twins game was tight, the kind where 54% confidence means you're really picking the slightly better coin flip. The Dodgers miss stung a bit more at 61%, but that's September baseball. Teams are fighting for positioning, rotations are shuffling, and sometimes the underdog just has more to prove that day.

## Tomorrow's Story: Back to Pittsburgh

Here's what caught my eye for September 17th: the Brewers are heading back to Pittsburgh. Yes, we liked Milwaukee yesterday at 61%, and yes, we're back on them tomorrow—though this time with a more modest 52% confidence.

Kyle Harrison takes the ball for the Brewers against Wilber Dotel and the Pirates. This is one of those matchups where the model sees just enough edge to lean Milwaukee's way, but it's acknowledging this could go either way.

## Why Milwaukee Again?

The Brewers showed us yesterday they can handle PNC Park. Kyle Harrison has been steady enough to trust in this spot, and while 52% isn't screaming conviction, it's saying "if we had to pick, this is the side we'd want."

Pittsburgh's fighting, they always do at home, but the Brewers have the pitching edge and just enough momentum from yesterday's win to make this interesting.

It's not the slam dunk some of yesterday's 61% picks were, but that's tomorrow for you—a clean slate where a narrow edge might be all you need.

## The Bottom Line

11-4 feels good. Really good. It's the kind of day that validates the late nights, the data checks, the model refinements. But here's the thing about September baseball—every day is its own story.

Tomorrow we're backing the Brewers with modest confidence, and we'll see if Kyle Harrison can author another chapter in Milwaukee's push toward October.

Let's see what September 17th brings. ⚾

author: Hana
